### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.animate

### Question

Hi everyone,

I binded '<' and '>' to '<gv' and '>gv', but I found that 'gv' operation would be cancelled or overrided after enabling scroll animation, especially when it crossed multiple lines. Does anyone know how to solve it? Thanks

here is the keybind
```
:verbose vmap
v  <           * <gv
                 Indent line(s) less
v  >           * >gv
                 Indent line(s) more
```

and here is my super easy config
```lua
    local animate = require('mini.animate')
    animate.setup({
      resize = { enable = false },
      open = { enable = false },
      close = { enable = false },
      cursor = { enable = false },
      scroll = {
        enable = true,
        timing = animate.gen_timing.linear({ duration = 10, unit = 'total' }),
        subscroll = animate.gen_subscroll.equal({ max_output_steps = 5 }),
      },
    })
```

comment_data.body:
As scroll animation is [done with side effects](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-animate.html#minianimate.config.scroll), there has to be some workarounds to achieve this. They require performing `>` / `<` before scroll animation while executing `gv` after.

There are couple of methods here:
- Go the route documented above which requires usage of [`execute_after()`](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-animate.html#minianimate.execute_after). Something like this seems to work:

    ```lua
    vim.keymap.set('x', '>', '<Cmd>lua vim.cmd("normal! >"); MiniAnimate.execute_after("scroll", "normal! gv")<CR>')
    vim.keymap.set('x', '<', '<Cmd>lua vim.cmd("normal! <"); MiniAnimate.execute_after("scroll", "normal! gv")<CR>')
    ```

- Explicitly temporarily disable animation when performing mapping's action. This is a more general approach and can be done like this:

    ```lua
    local enable_animate_later = vim.schedule_wrap(function() vim.b.minianimate_disable = nil end)
    local map_without_animate = function(mode, lhs, rhs, opts)
      local new_rhs = function()
        vim.b.minianimate_disable = true
        enable_animate_later()
        return rhs
      end
      opts = opts or {}
      opts.expr = true
      vim.keymap.set(mode, lhs, new_rhs, opts)
    end

    map_without_animate('x', '>', '>gv')
    map_without_animate('x', '<', '<gv')
    ```

**However**, my sincere suggestion would be to use ['mini.move'](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/readmes/mini-move.html) (it provides this type of repeatable Visual mode indentation with some extra usability touches) or not use scroll animation (as it is too disruptive of how Neovim works in general).
